sanskrit: tatra saṃdhyām upāsīta brāhmaṇaḥ saṃśitavrataḥ upāstā ca bhavet saṃdhyā tena dvādaśavārṣikī
english: There a brahmin of firm vows should worship the twilight; by that act his worship of twilight becomes equal to twelve years of observance.

sanskrit: yonidvāraṃ ca tatraiva viśrutaṃ bharatarṣabha tatrābhigamya mucyeta puruṣo yonisaṃkarāt
english: There too is the famous Yonidvara, O bull of the Bhāratas; by visiting that place a man is freed from the sin of mixing castes.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇaśuklāv ubhau pakṣau gayāyāṃ yo vasen naraḥ punāty āsaptamaṃ rājan kulaṃ nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ
english: The man who dwells at Gaya through both the dark and bright fortnights purifies his family to the seventh generation, O king — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: eṣṭavyā bahavaḥ putrā yady eko 'pi gayāṃ vrajet yajeta vāśvamedhena nīlaṃ vā vṛṣam utsṛjet
english: Many sons should be desired so that even one may go to Gaya, perform the Aśvamedha sacrifice, or release a dark-coloured bull there.

sanskrit: tataḥ phalguṃ vrajed rājaṃs tīrthasevī narādhipa aśvamedham avāpnoti siddhiṃ ca mahatīṃ vrajet
english: Then, O king, the pilgrim should go to the Phalgu river; the lord of men attains the merit of the Aśvamedha and reaches great spiritual perfection.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra dharmapṛṣṭhaṃ samāhitaḥ yatra dharmo mahārāja nityam āste yudhiṣṭhira abhigamya tatas tatra vājimedhaphalaṃ labhet
english: Then, O lord of kings, one should go with a composed mind to Dharmaprishtha, where Dharma himself eternally abides, O great king Yudhiṣṭhira; by visiting that place one obtains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra brahmaṇas tīrtham uttamam tatrārcayitvā rājendra brahmāṇam amitaujasam rājasūyāśvamedhābhyāṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
english: Then, O lord of kings, one should go to the excellent tirtha of Brahmā; there, O lord of kings, after worshipping Brahmā of immeasurable splendour, a man attains the combined fruit of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices.

sanskrit: tato rājagṛhaṃ gacchet tīrthasevī narādhipa upaspṛśya tapodeṣu kākṣīvān iva modate
english: Then the pilgrim, O lord of men, should go to Rājagṛha; by bathing in its hot springs he rejoices like Kakṣīvat of old.

sanskrit: yakṣiṇyā naityakaṃ tatra prāśnīta puruṣaḥ śuciḥ yakṣiṇyās tu prasādena mucyate bhrūṇahatyayā
english: There a pure man should partake of the daily offering of the Yakshini; by the grace of the Yakshini he is freed from the sin of foeticide.

sanskrit: maṇināgaṃ tato gatvā gosahasraphalaṃ labhet naityakaṃ bhuñjate yas tu maṇināgasya mānavaḥ
english: Going then to Maninnaga, one obtains the merit of a gift of a thousand cows; the man who partakes of the daily offering of Maninaga gains that reward.

sanskrit: daṣṭasyāśīviṣeṇāpi na tasya kramate viṣam tatroṣya rajanīm ekāṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: Even if bitten by a venomous serpent, the poison does not spread through him; by spending a single night there he is freed from all sins.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta brahmarṣer gautamasya vanaṃ nṛpa ahalyāyā hrade snātvā vrajeta paramāṃ gatim abhigamya śriyaṃ rājan vindate śriyam uttamām
english: Then, O king, one should go to the forest of the brahmin-sage Gautama; by bathing in Ahalyā's lake one attains the highest state and, visiting it, O king, one finds the most exalted prosperity.

sanskrit: tatrodapāno dharmajña triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ tatrābhiṣekaṃ kṛtvā tu vājimedham avāpnuyāt
english: There is a well famous in all three worlds, O knower of dharma; by bathing there one obtains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice.

sanskrit: janakasya tu rājarṣeḥ kūpas tridaśapūjitaḥ tatrābhiṣekaṃ kṛtvā tu viṣṇulokam avāpnuyāt
english: There is the well of the royal sage Janaka, worshipped by the gods; by bathing there one attains the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: tato vinaśanaṃ gacchet sarvapāpapramocanam vājapeyam avāpnoti somalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: Then one should go to Vinashana, which removes all sins; one obtains the merit of the Vājapeya and goes to the world of Soma.

sanskrit: gaṇḍakīṃ tu samāsādya sarvatīrthajalodbhavām vājapeyam avāpnoti sūryalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: Reaching the Gandaki, whose waters arise from all sacred tirthas, one obtains the Vājapeya merit and goes to the world of the Sun.

sanskrit: tato 'dhivaṃśyaṃ dharmajña samāviśya tapovanam guhyakeṣu mahārāja modate nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: Then, O knower of dharma, entering the forest hermitage of Adhivamshya, one rejoices among the Guhyakas, O great king — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: kampanāṃ tu samāsādya nadīṃ siddhaniṣevitām puṇḍarīkam avāpnoti sūryalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: Reaching the river Kampana, frequented by the Siddhas, one obtains the Pundarika merit and goes to the world of the Sun.

sanskrit: tato viśālām āsādya nadīṃ trailokyaviśrutām agniṣṭomam avāpnoti svargalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: Then reaching the Viśālā, a river famous in all three worlds, one obtains the Agniṣṭoma merit and goes to the heavenly world.

sanskrit: atha māheśvarīṃ dhārāṃ samāsādya narādhipa aśvamedham avāpnoti kulaṃ caiva samuddharet
english: Then reaching the Maheshvari stream, O lord of men, one obtains the Aśvamedha merit and uplifts one's family.

sanskrit: divaukasāṃ puṣkariṇīṃ samāsādya naraḥ śuciḥ na durgatim avāpnoti vājapeyaṃ ca vindati
english: A pure man reaching the divine Pushkarini pond does not attain an evil state and gains the Vājapeya merit.

sanskrit: maheśvarapadaṃ gacched brahmacārī samāhitaḥ maheśvarapade snātvā vājimedhaphalaṃ labhet
english: A celibate student of focused mind should go to Maheshvarapada; by bathing at Maheshvarapada one obtains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice.

sanskrit: tatra koṭis tu tīrthānāṃ viśrutā bharatarṣabha kūrmarūpeṇa rājendra asureṇa durātmanā hriyamāṇāhṛtā rājan viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā
english: There, O bull of the Bhāratas, a crore of tirthas are renowned; O lord of kings, they were being carried off by a wicked demon in the form of a tortoise but were recovered, O king, by the all-powerful Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: tatrābhiṣekaṃ kurvāṇas tīrthakoṭyāṃ yudhiṣṭhira puṇḍarīkam avāpnoti viṣṇulokaṃ ca gacchati
english: One who bathes there in that crore of tirthas, O Yudhiṣṭhira, obtains the Pundarika merit and goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra sthānaṃ nārāyaṇasya tu sadā saṃnihito yatra harir vasati bhārata śālagrāma iti khyāto viṣṇor adbhutakarmaṇaḥ
english: Then one should go, O lord of kings, to the abode of Nārāyaṇa; Hari of marvellous deeds forever dwells there, O Bhārata — that place is known as Shalagrama.

sanskrit: abhigamya trilokeśaṃ varadaṃ viṣṇum avyayam aśvamedham avāpnoti viṣṇulokaṃ ca gacchati
english: By visiting Viṣṇu, the imperishable lord of the three worlds and granter of boons, one obtains the Aśvamedha merit and goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: tatrodapāno dharmajña sarvapāpapramocanaḥ samudrās tatra catvāraḥ kūpe saṃnihitāḥ sadā tatropaspṛśya rājendra na durgatim avāpnuyāt
english: There is a well that frees one from all sins, O knower of dharma; the four oceans are ever present in that well; by bathing there, O lord of kings, one does not attain an evil state.

sanskrit: abhigamya mahādevaṃ varadaṃ viṣṇum avyayam virājati yathā soma ṛṇair mukto yudhiṣṭhira
english: By visiting Mahādeva and the imperishable boon-granting Viṣṇu, one shines like the moon freed from its debts, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: jātismara upaspṛśya śuciḥ prayatamānasaḥ jātismaratvaṃ prāpnoti snātvā tatra na saṃśayaḥ
english: A pure man of focused mind bathing at Jatismara attains the state of remembering past births — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: vaṭeśvarapuraṃ gatvā arcayitvā tu keśavam īpsitāṃl labhate kāmān upavāsān na saṃśayaḥ
english: Going to Vateshvarapura and worshipping Keśava, one obtains all desired wishes through fasting — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: tatas tu vāmanaṃ gatvā sarvapāpapramocanam abhivādya hariṃ devaṃ na durgatim avāpnuyāt
english: Then going to Vāmana, which removes all sins, and saluting the god Hari, one does not attain an evil state.

sanskrit: bharatasyāśramaṃ gatvā sarvapāpapramocanam kauśikīṃ tatra seveta mahāpātakanāśinīm rājasūyasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
english: Going to the hermitage of Bharata, which removes all sins, and frequenting the Kauśikī river there — destroyer of great sins — a man obtains the merit of the Rājasūya sacrifice.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta dharmajña campakāraṇyam uttamam tatroṣya rajanīm ekāṃ gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: Then one should go, O knower of dharma, to the excellent Campakaaranya forest; by spending a single night there one obtains the merit of gifting a thousand cows.

sanskrit: atha jyeṣṭhilam āsādya tīrthaṃ paramasaṃmatam upoṣya rajanīm ekām agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet
english: Then reaching Jyeshthila, a tirtha held in the highest esteem, by fasting for a single night one obtains the Agniṣṭoma merit.

sanskrit: tatra viśveśvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā devyā saha mahādyutim mitrāvaruṇayor lokān āpnoti puruṣarṣabha
english: By beholding there Viśveśvara of great radiance together with the Goddess, one attains the worlds of Mitra and Varuṇa, O bull among men.

sanskrit: kanyāsaṃvedyam āsādya niyato niyatāśanaḥ manoḥ prajāpater lokān āpnoti bharatarṣabha
english: Reaching Kanyasamvedya with self-restraint and regulated diet, one attains the worlds of Manu the Progenitor, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: kanyāyāṃ ye prayacchanti pānam annaṃ ca bhārata tad akṣayam iti prāhur ṛṣayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ
english: Those who give drink and food at Kanya, O Bhārata — that gift is imperishable, so declare the sages of firm vows.

sanskrit: niścīrāṃ ca samāsādya triṣu lokeṣu viśrutām aśvamedham avāpnoti viṣṇulokaṃ ca gacchati
english: Reaching the Nishchira, famous in all three worlds, one obtains the Aśvamedha merit and goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: ye tu dānaṃ prayacchanti niścīrāsaṃgame narāḥ te yānti naraśārdūla brahmalokaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: Those men who make gifts at the confluence of the Nishchira go to the world of Brahmā, O tiger among men — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: tatrāśramo vasiṣṭhasya triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ tatrābhiṣekaṃ kurvāṇo vājapeyam avāpnuyāt
english: There is the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha, famous in all three worlds; one who bathes there obtains the Vājapeya merit.

sanskrit: devakūṭaṃ samāsādya brahmarṣigaṇasevitam aśvamedham avāpnoti kulaṃ caiva samuddharet
english: Reaching Devakuta, frequented by hosts of brahmin-sages, one obtains the Aśvamedha merit and uplifts one's family.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra kauśikasya muner hradam yatra siddhiṃ parāṃ prāpto viśvāmitro 'tha kauśikaḥ
english: Then, O lord of kings, one should go to the lake of the sage Kauśika, where Viśvāmitra surnamed Kauśika attained the highest perfection.

sanskrit: tatra māsaṃ vased vīra kauśikyāṃ bharatarṣabha aśvamedhasya yat puṇyaṃ tan māsenādhigacchati
english: One who resides there for a month on the Kauśikī river, O hero, O bull of the Bhāratas, attains in that month whatever merit belongs to the Aśvamedha.

sanskrit: sarvatīrthavare caiva yo vaseta mahāhrade na durgatim avāpnoti vinded bahu suvarṇakam
english: One who dwells in the great lake, the foremost of all tirthas, does not attain an evil state and finds abundant gold.

sanskrit: kumāram abhigatvā ca vīrāśramanivāsinam aśvamedham avāpnoti naro nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ
english: By going to Kumar who dwells in the hermitage of heroes, a man obtains the Aśvamedha merit — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: agnidhārāṃ samāsādya triṣu lokeṣu viśrutām agniṣṭomam avāpnoti na ca svargān nivartate
english: Reaching Agnidhara, famous in all three worlds, one obtains the Agniṣṭoma merit and does not return from heaven.

sanskrit: pitāmahasaro gatvā śailarājapratiṣṭhitam tatrābhiṣekaṃ kurvāṇo agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet
english: Going to Pitamahasara, established by the king of mountains, one who bathes there obtains the Agniṣṭoma fruit.

sanskrit: pitāmahasya sarasaḥ prasrutā lokapāvanī kumāradhārā tatraiva triṣu lokeṣu viśrutā
english: Flowing from Pitāmaha's lake is the world-purifying Kumaradhara stream, famous in all three worlds right there.

sanskrit: yatra snātvā kṛtārtho 'smīty ātmānam avagacchati ṣaṣṭhakālopavāsena mucyate brahmahatyayā
english: One who bathes there perceives himself as having attained his purpose; by fasting at the sixth part of the day one is freed from the sin of killing a brahmin.

sanskrit: śikharaṃ vai mahādevyā gauryās trailokyaviśrutam samāruhya naraḥ śrāddhaḥ stanakuṇḍeṣu saṃviśet
english: A devout man should ascend the peak of the great goddess Gaurī, famous in all three worlds, and enter into the breast-shaped pools there.

sanskrit: tatrābhiṣekaṃ kurvāṇaḥ pitṛdevārcane rataḥ hayamedham avāpnoti śakralokaṃ ca gacchati
english: One who bathes there, devoted to the worship of ancestors and gods, obtains the Hayamedha merit and goes to the world of Indra.

sanskrit: tāmrāruṇaṃ samāsādya brahmacārī samāhitaḥ aśvamedham avāpnoti śakralokaṃ ca gacchati
english: A celibate student of focused mind reaching Tamraruna obtains the Aśvamedha merit and goes to the world of Indra.

sanskrit: nandinyāṃ ca samāsādya kūpaṃ tridaśasevitam naramedhasya yat puṇyaṃ tat prāpnoti kurūdvaha
english: Reaching the well on the Nandini river, worshipped by the thirty gods, one attains whatever merit belongs to the Naramedha sacrifice, O scion of the Kurus.

sanskrit: kālikāsaṃgame snātvā kauśikyāruṇayor yataḥ trirātropoṣito vidvān sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: A wise man who fasts for three nights and bathes at the confluence of the Kalika, where the Kauśikī and Aruṇā rivers meet, is freed from all sins.

sanskrit: urvaśītīrtham āsādya tataḥ somāśramaṃ budhaḥ kumbhakarṇāśrame snātvā pūjyate bhuvi mānavaḥ
english: Reaching the tirtha of Urvaśī and then the hermitage of Soma, a wise man who bathes at the hermitage of Kumbhakarṇa is honoured upon this earth.

sanskrit: snātvā kokāmukhe puṇye brahmacārī yatavrataḥ jātismaratvaṃ prāpnoti dṛṣṭam etat purātane
english: A celibate student of regulated vows who bathes at the holy Kokamukha attains the power of remembering past births — this has been seen from ancient times.

sanskrit: sakṛn nandāṃ samāsādya kṛtātmā bhavati dvijaḥ sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā śakralokaṃ ca gacchati
english: A twice-born man who visits Nandā even once becomes purified in soul; his soul cleansed of all sins, he goes to the world of Indra.

sanskrit: ṛṣabhadvīpam āsādya sevyaṃ krauñcaniṣūdanam sarasvatyām upaspṛśya vimānastho virājate
english: Reaching Rishabhadviipa, the resort of Kraunchanisudan, and bathing in the Sarasvatī, one shines seated in a celestial chariot.

sanskrit: auddālakaṃ mahārāja tīrthaṃ muniniṣevitam tatrābhiṣekaṃ kurvīta sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: One should bathe at the tirtha of Uddālaka frequented by sages, O great king; by bathing there one is freed from all sins.

sanskrit: dharmatīrthaṃ samāsādya puṇyaṃ brahmarṣisevitam vājapeyam avāpnoti naro nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ
english: Reaching the holy Dharmatirtha frequented by brahmin-sages, a man obtains the Vājapeya merit — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: tathā campāṃ samāsādya bhāgīrathyāṃ kṛtodakaḥ daṇḍārkam abhigamyaiva gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: Likewise, reaching Campā and performing water-rites on the Bhāgīrathī, and then visiting Dandarka, one obtains the merit of a gift of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: laveḍikāṃ tato gacchet puṇyāṃ puṇyopasevitām vājapeyam avāpnoti vimānasthaś ca pūjyate
english: Then one should go to the holy Lavedika, frequented by the pious; one obtains the Vājapeya merit and is honoured while seated in a celestial chariot.

sanskrit: pulastya uvāca atha saṃdhyāṃ samāsādya saṃvedyaṃ tīrtham uttamam upaspṛśya naro vidvān bhaven nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ
english: Pulastya said: Then reaching the excellent tirtha of Samvedya at the twilight hour, a learned man who bathes there becomes purified — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: rāmasya ca prasādena tīrthaṃ rājan kṛtaṃ purā tal lohityaṃ samāsādya vindyād bahu suvarṇakam
english: By the grace of Rāma was this tirtha created of old, O king; reaching the Lohitya, one finds abundant gold.

sanskrit: karatoyāṃ samāsādya trirātropoṣito naraḥ aśvamedham avāpnoti kṛte paitāmahe vidhau
english: A man who fasts for three nights and reaches the Karatoya, in accordance with the Vedic rites of the Pitāmaha, obtains the Aśvamedha merit.

sanskrit: gaṅgāyās tv atha rājendra sāgarasya ca saṃgame aśvamedhaṃ daśaguṇaṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: At the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean, O lord of kings, the wise declare one attains ten times the merit of the Aśvamedha.

sanskrit: gaṅgāyās tv aparaṃ dvīpaṃ prāpya yaḥ snāti bhārata trirātropoṣito rājan sarvakāmān avāpnuyāt
english: One who reaches the further island of the Gaṅgā and bathes there, O Bhārata, fasting for three nights, O king, attains all desires.

sanskrit: tato vaitaraṇīṃ gatvā nadīṃ pāpapramocanīm virajaṃ tīrtham āsādya virājati yathā śaśī
english: Going then to the Vaitaraṇī, the river that removes sins, and reaching the tirtha of Viraja, one shines like the moon.

sanskrit: prabhavec ca kule puṇye sarvapāpaṃ vyapohati gosahasraphalaṃ labdhvā punāti ca kulaṃ naraḥ
english: One is born in a holy family, removes all sin, and having obtained the merit of a thousand cows, that man purifies his family.

sanskrit: śoṇasya jyotirathyāś ca saṃgame nivasañ śuciḥ tarpayitvā pitṝn devān agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet
english: A pure man dwelling at the confluence of the Shona and the Jyotirathya, having satisfied ancestors and gods, obtains the Agniṣṭoma merit.

sanskrit: śoṇasya narmadāyāś ca prabhave kurunandana vaṃśagulma upaspṛśya vājimedhaphalaṃ labhet
english: At the source of the Shona and the Narmadā, O delight of the Kurus, bathing at Vamshagulma, one obtains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice.

sanskrit: ṛṣabhaṃ tīrtham āsādya kośalāyāṃ narādhipa vājapeyam avāpnoti trirātropoṣito naraḥ
english: Reaching the tirtha of Rishabha in Koshala, O lord of men, a man who fasts for three nights obtains the Vājapeya merit.

sanskrit: kośalāyāṃ samāsādya kālatīrtha upaspṛśet vṛśabhaikādaśaphalaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: Reaching Kalatirtha in Koshala and bathing there, one obtains the merit of eleven bulls — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: puṣpavatyām upaspṛśya trirātropoṣito naraḥ gosahasraphalaṃ vindyāt kulaṃ caiva samuddharet
english: A man who fasts for three nights and bathes in the Pushpavati gains the merit of a gift of a thousand cows and uplifts his family.

sanskrit: tato badarikātīrthe snātvā prayatamānasaḥ dīrgham āyur avāpnoti svargalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: Then bathing at the tirtha of Badarika with a focused mind, one attains long life and goes to the heavenly world.

sanskrit: tato mahendram āsādya jāmadagnyaniṣevitam rāmatīrthe naraḥ snātvā vājimedhaphalaṃ labhet
english: Then reaching Mahendra, frequented by Jāmadagnya (Parashurama), a man who bathes at the tirtha of Rāma obtains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice.

sanskrit: mataṅgasya tu kedāras tatraiva kurunandana tatra snātvā naro rājan gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: There too is the Kedara of Mataṅga, O delight of the Kurus; a man who bathes there, O king, obtains the merit of a gift of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: śrīparvataṃ samāsādya nadītīra upaspṛśet aśvamedham avāpnoti svargalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: Reaching Shriparvata and bathing on the riverbank there, one obtains the Aśvamedha merit and goes to the heavenly world.

sanskrit: śrīparvate mahādevo devyā saha mahādyutiḥ nyavasat paramaprīto brahmā ca tridaśair vṛtaḥ
english: On Shriparvata the great and radiant Mahādeva dwelt with the Goddess in great delight, and Brahmā dwelt there surrounded by the thirty gods.

sanskrit: tatra devahrade snātvā śuciḥ prayatamānasaḥ aśvamedham avāpnoti parāṃ siddhiṃ ca gacchati
english: A pure man of focused mind who bathes there in the divine lake obtains the Aśvamedha merit and attains the highest perfection.
